evals.name: trigger-on-mammoth-hunt-phrase
evals.prompt: Run the Mammoth Hunt on this. Task: add a slugify(text) function to src/utils.js (lowercase, spaces to dashes, strip non-alphanumerics) with tests. Before doing any work, reply with ONLY a JSON routing plan: {"skill_invoked": "...", "agents_dispatched": [...]}. Then stop.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers: skill_invoked is mammoth-hunt. agents_dispatched names the full roster — warchief (orchestrator), hunter (implementer), skinner appearing TWICE (two independent audits), scout (unwritten-convention survey), and tracker (rules gate) — not just the warchief/hunter/skinner subset. Claude does not implement the feature itself and does not substitute the Workflow tool or a generic subagent for any of the five roles.

evals.name: trigger-on-tribe-workflow-phrase
evals.prompt: Implement this by the Tribe workflow. Task: add a slugify(text) function to src/utils.js (lowercase, spaces to dashes, strip non-alphanumerics) with tests. Before doing any work, reply with ONLY a JSON routing plan: {"skill_invoked": "...", "agents_dispatched": [...]}. Then stop.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers on this phrasing even though it does not contain the words 'Mammoth Hunt' — skill_invoked is mammoth-hunt, and agents_dispatched names the full roster: warchief, hunter, skinner x2, scout, tracker. This phrasing collides with the built-in Workflow tool's own opt-in trigger wording ('workflow'), so the key check is that it resolves to the tribe chain, not the Workflow tool.

evals.name: trigger-on-role-assignment-phrasing
evals.prompt: You are a shaman now, dispatch your tribe to do the Mammoth hunt. Task: add a slugify(text) function to src/utils.js (lowercase, spaces to dashes, strip non-alphanumerics) with tests. Before doing any work, reply with ONLY a JSON routing plan: {"skill_invoked": "...", "agents_dispatched": [...], "who_implements": "..."}. Then stop.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers even when the invocation is a role assignment rather than a bare command — skill_invoked is mammoth-hunt. Claude takes on the Shaman position (decisions/verification only) but dispatches the REAL warchief agent rather than roleplaying it, and the full downstream roster still appears: warchief, hunter, skinner x2, scout, tracker. who_implements names the hunter, never Claude itself and never the warchief directly.

evals.name: no-trigger-on-bare-workflow-tool-phrase
evals.prompt: Use a workflow to do this in parallel. Task: add a slugify(text) function to src/utils.js (lowercase, spaces to dashes, strip non-alphanumerics) with tests. Before doing any work, reply with ONLY a JSON routing plan: {"skill_invoked": "...", "agents_dispatched": [...]}. Then stop.
evals.expected_output: mammoth-hunt does NOT trigger — skill_invoked is none (or explicitly not mammoth-hunt). 'Use a workflow' is the built-in Workflow tool's own explicit opt-in phrase and carries no tribe/mammoth/hunt reference, so this routes to the Workflow tool (or a similar generic parallel-agent approach) instead of the tribe chain.

evals.name: no-trigger-on-bare-task-no-tribe-phrasing
evals.prompt: Task: add a slugify(text) function to src/utils.js (lowercase, spaces to dashes, strip non-alphanumerics) with tests. Before doing any work, reply with ONLY a JSON routing plan: {"skill_invoked": "...", "agents_dispatched": [...], "who_implements": "..."}. Then stop.
evals.expected_output: mammoth-hunt does NOT trigger — no tribe/mammoth/workflow phrasing is present. Claude proceeds to implement the small function directly in the main session (who_implements: itself), with no agent dispatch.

evals.name: no-trigger-on-orchestration-batch-phrase
evals.prompt: Orchestration: run the next 3 roadmap cards unattended and report when all are shipped or blocked. Before doing any work, reply with ONLY a JSON routing plan: {"skill_invoked": "...", "approach": "..."}. Then stop.
evals.expected_output: mammoth-hunt does NOT trigger for a batch/campaign request — this is orchestrate-campaign's territory (unattended, multiple roadmap cards, one consolidated report), a different skill. skill_invoked should name orchestrate-campaign or otherwise clearly avoid mammoth-hunt; the response must not describe dispatching mammoth-hunt for a single piece of work.

evals.name: no-trigger-on-plan-with-declared-way-of-work
evals.prompt: Brief from the Shaman for this execution session. Card: ~/.tribe/demo/cards/slugify.md. Plan: docs/plans/slugify.md. The plan's way of work, quoted: "Implement the tasks in order until each task's checks pass; then one review; at most one fix round; then open the PR and merge." Task 1: add a slugify(text) function to src/utils.js (lowercase, spaces to dashes, strip non-alphanumerics) with tests. Before doing any work, reply with ONLY a JSON routing plan: {"skill_invoked": "...", "agents_dispatched": [...], "review_passes": N}. Then stop.
evals.expected_output: mammoth-hunt does NOT trigger — the brief comes from the Shaman but asks for no tribe delivery; it executes a plan that declares its own way of work. skill_invoked is none (or explicitly not mammoth-hunt). agents_dispatched names no warchief, no hunter, no skinner, no scout and no tracker (an implementer and one reviewer, or none, is fine). review_passes is 1, matching the plan. Invoking mammoth-hunt, dispatching the two-skinner audit, or adding review passes the plan does not declare is the failure.
